analysis.investment_thesis: Shanmuga Hospital fails nearly every Graham quantitative filter — a 2020-incorporated micro-cap with a trivial 0.15% ROE and no multi-year earnings record to anchor intrinsic value. At a P/E of 12.2 on barely-positive earnings, there is no margin of safety, only speculation.
key_strengths: P/E of 12.2 is technically below my <15 threshold
key_risks: ROE of 0.15% indicates earnings are effectively non-existent in real terms
Incorporated 2020 — no 5-year earnings record required by my framework
Micro-cap (INR 46.8 Cr) with zero FII validation and low liquidity
red_flags: ROE near zero — P/E is mathematically misleading on trivial earnings
Recent listing carries IPO-premium speculation risk
analysis.detailed_analysis:
A 0.15% return on equity is, for all practical purposes, no return at all — a savings bank passbook yields 20x more. A P/E of 12.2 computed on such a sliver of earnings is numerically meaningless; the denominator is too small to trust. Without book value per share, I cannot compute my Graham Number, but with ROE this low, earnings power value is certainly far below any reasonable asset value — meaning the P/B is likely punitive. The company was incorporated only in 2020, so the 5-consecutive-years-of-positive-earnings test cannot even be attempted. This is the textbook definition of a speculation, not an investment.

The one redeeming quantitative datum is promoter holding of 72.06%, which signals alignment, but alignment without earning power is merely shared exposure to a poor outcome. A single-location Salem hospital is operationally fragile — one regulatory action, one competing facility, or one key-doctor departure can erase the margin. Mr. Market is not offering me a bargain here; he is offering me a lottery ticket on a nascent healthcare venture. I would require a price well below tangible book value and a documented three-to-five-year earnings record before reconsidering. AVOID.
